name: Australia
source: WIA Australian Amateur Radio Band Plan, Revision 2026-1, February 2026. wia.org.au. 2 m, 70 cm and 23 cm: WIA Australian Amateur Radio Band Plan, Revision 2026-1, February 2026 (2 m, 70 cm and 23 cm tables and centres of activity). wia.org.au Receiver bands (not amateur): summarised from the ITU Radio Regulations Article 5 table of allocations and general knowledge of national use. Broad, and not specific to a licence.
note: Australia has no 60 m allocation. Shows the Advanced licence: 160, 80 (top part), 30, 17 and 12 m are Advanced only, and 20 and 6 m are Advanced and Standard. 3700-3776 kHz is not available. 30 m voice is domestic only, with the USB dial below 10128 kHz. WSPR on 20 m is shown at the worldwide 14095.6, though WIA's text says 14094.6. On VHF and UHF: 2 m is primary for all licences. 70 cm is secondary for all licensees, with no protection from LIPDs on 433.05-434.79 MHz. 23 cm is secondary, for Standard and Advanced only, and ITU 5.332A could bring power limits on 1258-1296 MHz if GNSS interference is reported. Digital voice calling is 439.200 MHz; the plan lists none on 2 m, where digital voice simplex is 144.7-144.8875 and 145.0625-145.2125 MHz, or on 23 cm, where simplex channels take analogue or digital. The 70 cm plan runs to 450 MHz, so check your radio's transmit limit. The non-amateur bands are only offered on a receiver, and a guide to what's where, not a statement of who may use it.
